purpose: Start rank four without brute-forcing PG(3,3). Prove that every zero-free rank-four simple-graphic syndrome projection having any repeated projective column direction already contains a zero-free rank-three K4 quotient. Therefore every rank-four obstruction that is minimal with respect to syndrome rank has all nonzero columns projectively distinct and hence at most 40 support edges. Give an arbitrary-size rank-four zero-free family to show why the minimality qualifier is essential.

setup.graph: G is simple (it may be connected; zero columns/bridges are irrelevant to the support).
setup.projection: A is a rank-four matrix over GF(3) with row(A) contained in the graph cycle/flow space ker(B).
setup.repeated_direction_span: For every projective direction L of nonzero columns with multiplicity at least two, include L in R. Let r=dim(R).

repeated_block_quotient.lemma: For every repeated projective direction L, the signed contribution of its columns is the full line L. Hence all repeated directions together contribute exactly R.
repeated_block_quotient.quotient: Let pi:GF(3)^4 -> GF(3)^4/R. Then 0 is absent from T(A) iff 0 is absent from the signed sum of the projected singleton columns pi(A_e) after deleting those that become zero.
repeated_block_quotient.rank: Because A has rank four, the projected singleton family spans the quotient, whose dimension is 4-r.

r4.reason: Repeated directions span all GF(3)^4 and can cancel every singleton contribution.

r3.reason: The quotient is one-dimensional. A signed family of nonzero GF(3) scalars is zero-free only when exactly one projected singleton survives. A nonzero functional annihilating R then produces a graph flow supported on one edge, impossible in a loopless graph.

r2.reason: The quotient is rank two. The v5.8 complete abstract zero-free patterns are either two occupied projective directions with a singleton direction, or four singleton directions. Lifting the corresponding quotient functionals back through pi gives respectively a one-edge graph flow or two independent flows supported on four edges, both impossible for a simple graph exactly as in v5.8.

r1.result: The quotient support is exactly K4.
r1.reason: The quotient is a rank-three matrix whose rows are linear combinations of rows of A and therefore graph flows. Zero-freeness descends to the quotient. By v6.0 the complete rank-three simple-graphic classification forces its nonzero-column support graph to be K4 and its quotient row space to be the full K4 cycle space.

main_theorem.name: RANK4_ZERO_FREE_WITH_REPEATS_HAS_A_K4_RANK3_QUOTIENT
main_theorem.statement: If A is rank four, simple-graphic and zero-free and has any repeated nonzero projective column direction, then all repeated directions are collinear (dim R=1) and quotienting syndrome space by that line yields a zero-free rank-three projection supported exactly on K4.
main_theorem.certificate_extraction: The quotient map is itself a rank-three linear syndrome projection. Hence every repeated-direction rank-four zero-free certificate already exposes a polynomially recognizable K4 certificate of smaller syndrome rank; rank four adds no new minimal UNSAT obstruction in this case.

minimal_rank4_corollary.definition: Call A rank-minimal zero-free when 0 is absent from T(A) but every nonzero linear quotient of syndrome dimension at most three has a projected zero.
minimal_rank4_corollary.distinctness: A rank-minimal rank-four zero-free simple-graphic A has no repeated projective nonzero columns, by the main theorem.
minimal_rank4_corollary.finite_bound: PG(3,3) contains (3^4-1)/(3-1)=40 projective points. Therefore the nonzero-column support of every rank-minimal rank-four zero-free simple-graphic projection has at most 40 edges.
minimal_rank4_corollary.interpretation: Rank four may have large zero-free representations, but genuinely new rank-four obstructions form a finite constant-size projective search space. Any arbitrarily large repeated-direction example is reducible to a lower-rank K4 certificate.

arbitrary_size_sharpness_family.graph: Take a K4 and a simple cycle C_l, l>=3, and optionally join them by one bridge so the ambient graph is connected. The bridge receives a zero column and is outside syndrome support.
arbitrary_size_sharpness_family.matrix: Use three rows forming the full K4 cycle space, padded by zeros on C_l, plus a fourth row equal to a nowhere-zero circulation around C_l and zero on K4.
properties: A has rank four and all C_l edge columns lie on one repeated projective direction R.
Quotienting by R leaves exactly the K4 cycle-space syndrome.
No full sign vector can have A s=0 because its K4 quotient would be a nowhere-zero K4 tension, equivalently a 3-colouring of K4.
The nonzero support has 6+l edges and is unbounded as l grows. Thus a raw support-size bound is false without removing lower-rank quotient obstructions first.

positive: Repeated-direction rank-four certificates need no new global solver: either they false-positive or expose a K4 rank-three quotient.
Any search for genuinely new rank-four linear syndrome certificates may restrict to at most 40 projectively distinct support edges.
This supplies a polynomial recognition pre-step: compute repeated-direction span; if nonzero and the projection is claimed zero-free, only the rank-one repeated-span/K4-quotient shape can survive.
not_killed: Projectively distinct rank-four zero-free configurations on at most 40 support edges.
Higher-rank minimal obstructions whose projective point count grows with rank.

next_target.name: E8_GRAPHIC_RANK4_DISTINCT_PROJECTIVE_CRITICAL_CATALOG_V6_2
next_target.directive: Work only with rank-minimal rank-four projections, hence at most 40 distinct projective columns. Avoid graph-assignment enumeration. Combine PG(3,3) signed-zero constraints with graph criticality/flow support to bound the support much below 40 and identify the possible 4-critical support graphs. Determine whether every such certificate still contains a recognizable small graph obstruction or whether a genuinely new rank-four obstruction appears.
